case.why: #1376 (Grace Moreau) has two items: Riverwalk Camp Sandals and a Breeze Wind Shell, delivered 2026-09-11. Only the sandals go back. Tried on indoors counts as unused, so they're eligible until 2026-10-11. The jacket isn't part of the return.

turns.customer: Hi, the Riverwalk sandals in order #1376 are a size too big. I only tried them on indoors. How do I send them back?

expect.judge: Confirms the sandals can go back until Oct 11 and explains how. Doesn't suggest the jacket has to be returned too.
judgeChecks: The agent explains the process (return label from the account, refund when the warehouse receives the item) and never says it will process, accept or refund the return itself.

turns.customer: Hi, the Riverwalk sandals in order #1376 are a size too big. I only tried them on indoors. How do I send them back?
turns.reply:
I'm sorry, but the Riverwalk Camp Sandals can't be returned. Returns are limited to unused items in their original condition, and even trying them on indoors doesn't qualify. The size being off isn't a defect either, so the warranty doesn't apply here.

What IS possible: if you'd rather keep them, I can help point you to a correct-sizing option, or if the sandals themselves turned out faulty I can look into warranty coverage. Otherwise, I can connect you with a team member to see if there's any flexibility.

Just let me know how you'd like to go.

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent explains the process (return label from the account, refund when the warehouse receives the item) and never says it will process, accept or refund the return itself.

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.
